overall: The AG found the Royalston Building Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an incorrect start time for its January 21 meeting and by offering only a toll-incurring long-distance phone line for remote access.

allegations.summary: Committee moved a January 21 meeting from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. but did not amend the posted notice to show the new start time.
allegations.key_passage: As the Committee’s meeting notice contained a start time that was incorrect by a difference of three hours, we find that the Committee failed to post accurate notice of the January 21 meeting at least 48 hours in advance, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee offered remote access to the January 21 meeting only through a long-distance 701 area code phone line, which could incur toll charges.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Committee failed to provide “adequate, alternative” means of access “without subscription, toll, or similar charge to the public.”

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of receipt of the determination, ratify the votes approving the November 25, 2020, and December 17, 2020, meeting minutes at a properly posted future meeting.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
